note:
A HANDOVER RECORD, NOT A DATA FILE. npc_roster's naming tables were removed when naming moved to the heritage language genome; what remains is a load-bearing gate that asserts the handover is complete. Carried whole from npc_roster/policies/names.json (852 bytes) because the gate is live and a port that drops it loses a real check, not because there is naming data here -- THERE IS NONE.

READ BY: npc_roster/policy.py:35 load() -> :45 load_all() -> :93 lint_names(). POLICY_FILES is ('posts', 'names'), so load_all ALWAYS reads and lints this file and a missing or malformed one makes load_all raise, which npc_roster.attach() turns into {'status': 'failed'} -- the whole roster block dies. Exactly four things are read: `revision` (policy.py:40 and :53 revisions(), exported as policy_revision.names), `supersede.package` (truthiness, :105), `supersede.status` (must equal the literal 'complete', :107), and the NEGATIVE check `'races' not in document` (:109). `schema`, `notes`, `supersede.signature` and `supersede.note` are read by nothing. tests/test_npc_roster.py:381+ exercises the checks.

RNG INPUT: no. ORDER IS FREE throughout -- `supersede` is three key lookups with no iteration and no index.

ABSENCE THAT IS NOT EMPTINESS, and it is INVERTED from every other field in this port: `races` MUST BE ABSENT. Its PRESENCE is the error (policy.py:109-110) -- the check exists to catch a half-reverted handover that puts the old syllable tables back. `supersede.status` must be exactly 'complete'; absent or any other value raises.

FOR THE PORT: carry the integer 2 as the `names` policy revision in whatever policy_revision structure you emit, then either keep the three-field gate or drop the file and hardcode the revision. Actual NPC naming is heritage.resolve / name_stock / stock_name -- see heritage-lexicon.json and heritage-name-draw.json.

PARSE-LEVEL RULES the loader applies and a port must keep: json.loads(text, object_pairs_hook=_pairs, parse_constant=_reject) -- DUPLICATE KEYS RAISE rather than last-wins, and NaN/Infinity RAISE rather than parse. `revision` must be an int >= 1.

IDENTITY HASH: NONE. No hashlib/sha256 call anywhere in this package touches this file, and the document carries no digest of its own -- provenance is the integer `revision` alone, republished into the world block. The nearest thing that transitively covers this content is the world handle, Sim/fantasy_world_generator/world_handle.py:80-82: sha256(json.dumps(transfer_document(doc), ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), allow_nan=False).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()[:16], prefixed 'w_'. It hashes the GENERATED OUTPUT, never these bytes -- and because sort_keys=True sorts mapping keys but NOT list elements, every list-order contract named above is load-bearing at the handle level while every mapping-key order is not. Note the codebase has three mutually disagreeing canonical forms and you must pick per call site, not per repository: registry_identity() (civilization_registry.py:308) ensure_ascii=False + separators + NO sort_keys; castle_planner.py:39 sort_keys=True + separators + ensure_ascii DEFAULT TRUE; heritage/derive.py:330 sort_keys=True + separators + ensure_ascii=False. `source_sha256` in this file is a plain digest of the source file's raw bytes, recorded for provenance only; nothing in the Python computes it.
source_note: This file no longer holds naming data. It is kept so policy_revision can still say which naming contract a roster was built against - revision 1 is interim parent-race tables, revision 2 is the heritage genome - which a consumer reading an older export needs in order to tell them apart. Do not add tables here; extend the genome.

supersede.note: Superseded on 2026-09-19. Names now come from the heritage genome keyed by civilization id. The interim parent-race tables are removed: they gave nine of the twelve cultures their parent’s names and gave tidekin, gnome, hill_dwarf and frosthold_dwarf human ones outright.
